item.title: Review the first month of a repair voucher
item.summary: Two council staff members disagree about what a drop in voucher claims tells them.
item.transcript_text:
Nadia: We handed out nearly all the repair vouchers, but fewer than half have been used. My first thought was that people changed their minds about repairing things.
Ben: The shops told us some customers arrived with items they couldn't fix. A shoe repair shop was listed as a general repair shop. Other customers were waiting for appointments beyond our deadline.
Nadia: So extending it might help, but it would not solve the shop list.
Ben: Right. I'd sort the claims by what people wanted to repair, call the shops about their capacity, and extend the deadline for people already on a waiting list.
Nadia: Let's hold off on printing another batch until we can see which change makes a difference.

questions.prompt: What are Nadia and Ben trying to decide?
options: Whether shoe repairs should cost more
How to respond to low voucher use
Where to open a public repair shop
How to choose a new printer
questions.explanation: They discuss why many distributed vouchers remain unused and what to change.

questions.prompt: Why did some customers fail to use a voucher?
options: The listed shops did not handle their repair
Shops refused to accept any vouchers
Most vouchers were already used
The council raised repair prices
questions.explanation: A shoe repair shop was listed too broadly.

questions.prompt: What does Nadia say an extension alone leaves unresolved?
options: The total number of vouchers handed out
Whether the printer is available
How people learned about the scheme
Misleading information about shop services
questions.explanation: Extra time cannot fix a list that points customers to the wrong specialist.

questions.prompt: Whom would Ben give more time?
options: Every shop employee
Only people needing shoe repairs
People already awaiting appointments
People applying for a new batch
questions.explanation: Ben proposes an extension for customers on waiting lists.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of delaying more printing?
options: To discontinue the scheme permanently
To learn which changes improve use first
To move the budget to advertising
To require a print-only registration
questions.explanation: Nadia wants to distinguish the effects of the proposed fixes.

children.segment_text: people changed their minds about repairing things
hold off on printing another batch
